newsitem.title: USA: Calif. banker says campaign violations were minor.
newsitem.headline: Calif. banker says campaign violations were minor.

text.p: Calvin Grigsby, whose firm is among the largest African American-owned municipal underwriters in the U.S., said Monday the press was exaggerating his campaign contribution violations.
"I don't consider this a major item," Grigsby told reporters at a Bond Buyer conference in San Francisco. "To me, it's not a big deal because it's just a reporting violation."

"Somehow, the press has made it look a lot more than that," he added. "Why that happens, I think, has a lot to do with their interest in the fact that I'm an African American ... I think there's some character assassination there."
The California Fair Political Practices Commission said Grigsby has paid a $5,000 fine for making campaign contributions without full and complete disclosure.
The case has attracted some local press attention.

The commission said Grigsby made campaign contributions totalling $11,500 in the first half of 1993. In the second half of 1993, Fiscal Funding Co and other entities controlled by Grigsby made campaign contributions totaling $42,000.
The commission said Grigsby and Fiscal Funding failed to file timely major donor campaign statements reporting these contributions.
Grigsby is a 50 percent owner and controlling partner of Fiscal Funding, an equipment leasing company.

In addition, the commission said Grigsby loaned money in December 1993 to Regina Bryant-Fields, who in turn contributed $4,500 to Alameda County Supervisor Mary King, who was then an Oakland, Calif., mayoral candidate.
"Grigsby knew or had reason to know that this loan would be used for the contribution to King, but neither Grigsby nor Bryant-Fields told King about the loan," the commission said.

The commission said making a campaign contribution without full and complete disclosure that the contribution was funded by a loan from a third party "undermines the campaign disclosure provisions of the Political Reform Act and it deprives the electorate of essential information about who is supporting a candidate."
Grigsby's firm, Grigsby Brandford & Co Inc of San Francisco, has handled several large municipal bond underwritings in Alameda County, the state commission said.
